title: Afro Bossa Salsa, Tootie for Cootie and the New Orleans Suite
summary: Dance recalls Cootie's records and pieces Duke wrote for him after his return.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, I'm just trying to think. Well, Procope and Paul. Of course you hadn't worked with Paul before. But anyway, it was still the band. Well, Cootie, right away, you made a record session which was wonderful. You made that "Afro Bossa Salsa".
Very nice. Then he did a number for you. "Tootie for Cootie".
Did he record that, do you know?
I don't know if we were recorded it or not. I think

Oh. And then, around in the beginning there, he wrote the "New Orleans Suite". Well, I don't know, that that wasn't in the beginning at that. But he wrote the "New Orleans Suite", and he had the tribute to Louie Armstrong in there that you played.
Remember? That was a beautiful thing.
